title: Dates
summary: Ask and give the date, say on which day something happens with the ordinals the first to the tenth, and put a week of plans in your calendar.
intro: To give the date in Arabic, say the day as an ordinal, then مِنْ (of), then the month: الْخَامِسُ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر (the fifth of November). The ordinal is masculine because it means 'the fifth day'. Be careful: the feminine ordinal is for the hour, so السَّابِعُ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر is a date, but السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة is seven o'clock. To ask the date, say مَا تَارِيخُ الْيَوْم؟
objectives: Ask مَا تَارِيخُ الْيَوْم؟ and answer it
Say a date with an ordinal from the first to the tenth
Tell the difference between السَّابِعُ (the seventh day) and السَّابِعَة (seven o'clock)
Put three plans in a calendar with their dates

realLife.title: The date on the board
realLife.story: Every morning Mr Karim writes the date on the board in Arabic. Today he asks the class to read it, and soon everyone is sharing important dates: Layla's party, the week test, little Nour's birthday and the trip to Amman. Daniel discovers that Americans and Egyptians don't even write dates the same way.

sentences.en: Today is the fifth of November.

mistakes.why: In standard Arabic the day is an ordinal followed by min: al-khāmisu min nūfambir, 'the fifth of November'.

sentences.en: The party is on the seventh of November.
sentences.literal: the party in the seventh of November

mistakes.why: In a date the ordinal is masculine, because it means 'the seventh day': as-sābiʿ. as-sābiʿa is for the hour: 'at seven o'clock'.

sentences.ar: عِيدُ مِيلَادِ نُور فِي الْأَوَّلِ مِنْ دِيسَمْبِر.
sentences.en: Nour's birthday is on the first of December.
sentences.literal: feast-of birth-of Nour in the first of December

sentences.en: I wrote the date in my phone's calendar.
sentences.literal: I-wrote the date in calendar-of my-phone

sentences.en: The tenth of December is a Wednesday.
sentences.literal: the tenth of December day-of Wednesday

dialogue.title: What's the date today?
dialogue.culture: In the Arab world dates are written day first, then month, as in Britain: ٧/١١ is the seventh of November. Many Arab countries use Arabic-Indic digits (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩), which are written from left to right like European digits, even inside right-to-left text. Official letters often give two dates: the Western one and the Islamic (Hijri) one.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر! قَبْلَ أَنْ نَبْدَأَ، مَنْ يَعْرِفُ تَارِيخَ الْيَوْم؟ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكْتُبَهُ عَلَى السَّبُّورَة.
lines.en: Good morning! Before we start, who knows today's date? I want to write it on the board.

lines.ar: الْيَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاء، الْخَامِسُ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر. أَنَا مُتَأَكِّدَة، لِأَنَّ حَفْلَتِي بَعْدَ يَوْمَيْنِ!
lines.en: Today is Wednesday, the fifth of November. I'm quite sure, because my party is in two days!

lines.ar: أَحْسَنْتِ يَا لَيْلَى. وَأَمْسِ كَانَ الرَّابِعَ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر، وَغَدًا سَيَكُونُ السَّادِسَ. هَلْ هٰذَا وَاضِح يَا دَانْيَال؟
lines.en: Well done, Layla. So yesterday was the fourth of November, and tomorrow will be the sixth. Is that clear, Daniel?

lines.ar: نَعَم، وَاضِح. لٰكِنْ فِي أَمْرِيكَا نَكْتُبُ التَّارِيخ بِطَرِيقَة أُخْرَى: الشَّهْر أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ الْيَوْم!
lines.en: Yes, it's clear. But in America we write the date another way: the month first, and then the day!

lines.ar: الشَّهْر أَوَّلًا؟ إِذَنْ أَنْتُمْ تَكْتُبُونَ ١١/٧ وَنَحْنُ نَكْتُبُ ٧/١١؟ هٰذَا مُرْبِك جِدًّا!
lines.en: The month first? So you write 11/7 and we write 7/11 for the same day? That's really confusing!

lines.ar: لِذٰلِكَ نَقْرَأُ التَّارِيخ بِالْكَلِمَات: الْيَوْم أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ «مِنْ»، ثُمَّ الشَّهْر. مَثَلًا: السَّابِعُ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر.
lines.en: That's why we read the date in words: first the day, then 'min' (of), then the month. For example: the seventh of November.

lines.ar: السَّابِعُ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر: هٰذَا يَوْمُ حَفْلَتِي! هَلْ كَتَبْتُمُ التَّارِيخ فِي تَقْوِيمِكُمْ؟
lines.en: The seventh of November: that's the day of my party! Have you all written the date in your calendars?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا! كَتَبْتُهُ فِي تَقْوِيمِ هَاتِفِي: الْجُمُعَة، السَّابِعُ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر، السَّاعَة السَّابِعَة مَسَاءً.
lines.en: Of course! I wrote it in my phone's calendar: Friday, the seventh of November, seven o'clock in the evening.

lines.ar: وَأَنَا عِنْدِي تَارِيخ مُهِمّ آخَر: الْأَوَّلُ مِنْ دِيسَمْبِر هُوَ عِيدُ مِيلَادِ أُخْتِي نُور. سَنَحْتَفِلُ فِي الْبَيْت مَعَ الْعَائِلَة كُلِّهَا.
lines.en: And I have another important date: the first of December is my sister Nour's birthday. We'll celebrate at home with the whole family.

lines.ar: جَمِيل! وَالْآنَ سُؤَال لِلْجَمِيع: مَتَى اِمْتِحَانُ الْأُسْبُوع؟ مَنْ يَتَذَكَّرُ التَّارِيخ؟
lines.en: Lovely! And now a question for everyone: when is the end-of-week test? Who remembers the date?

lines.ar: اِمْتِحَانُ الْأُسْبُوع يَوْمَ الْأَحَد، التَّاسِعِ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر، فِي السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة صَبَاحًا.
lines.en: The week test is on Sunday, the ninth of November, at ten o'clock in the morning.

lines.ar: يَوْمَ الْأَحَد؟ يَعْنِي بَعْدَ حَفْلَتِي بِيَوْمَيْنِ فَقَطْ! إِذَنْ سَنُرَاجِعُ مَعًا يَوْمَ السَّبْت، الثَّامِنِ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر.
lines.en: On Sunday? That means only two days after my party! So we'll revise together on Saturday, the eighth of November.

lines.ar: وَمَتَى سَتُسَافِرَانِ إِلَى عَمَّان يَا دَانْيَال؟ هَلْ عِنْدَكُمَا التَّذَاكِر؟
lines.en: And when are you two travelling to Amman, Daniel? Do you have your tickets yet?

lines.ar: لَيْسَ بَعْدُ. سَنَشْتَرِيهَا هٰذَا الْأُسْبُوعَ، وَسَنُسَافِرُ فِي دِيسَمْبِر، بَعْدَ عِيدِ مِيلَادِ نُور، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه.
lines.en: Not yet. We'll buy them this week, and we'll travel in December, after Nour's birthday, God willing.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز! إِذَنْ اُكْتُبُوا كُلَّ هٰذِهِ التَّوَارِيخ فِي تَقَاوِيمِكُمْ، وَلَا تَنْسَوْا شَيْئًا!
lines.en: Excellent! Then write all these dates in your calendars, and please don't forget anything!

reading.title: Daniel's calendar
reading.ar: فِي تَقْوِيمِ دَانْيَال تَوَارِيخ مُهِمَّة. يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة، السَّابِعِ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر، حَفْلَةُ عِيدِ مِيلَادِ لَيْلَى. يَوْمَ الْأَحَد، التَّاسِعِ مِنْ نُوفَمْبِر، اِمْتِحَانُ الْأُسْبُوع. فِي الْأَوَّلِ مِنْ دِيسَمْبِر عِيدُ مِيلَادِ نُور. وَبَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ سَيُسَافِرُ دَانْيَال وَلَيْلَى إِلَى عَمَّان.
reading.en: There are some important dates in Daniel's calendar. On Friday the seventh of November is Layla's birthday party. On Sunday the ninth of November is the week test. On the first of December is Nour's birthday. And after that Daniel and Layla will travel to Amman.

quiz.prompt: According to Daniel, what comes first when Americans write a date?
How is the article said in التَّاسِع (the ninth)?
options: at-tāsiʿ: the l joins the t, a sun letter

completion: Fantastic! You finished Week 8: you can talk about plans and the future, invitations, the weather, the seasons, the months and dates. Take the week test, and pass it with 80% to open Week 9.
